properties.value: Every key pair this tool generates is a Bitcoin secp256k1 keypair; ECDSA-secp256k1 is quantum-unsafe under Shor; the curve is fixed by the Bitcoin protocol — observable here, replaceable only ecosystem-wide. Enrichment: the escrow-code path (Model/EscrowCode.cs:105,175,263,355) is not plain pubkey derivation but a homegrown multiplicative 3-party key agreement — each party multiplies the running public point by their secret (Gxy = Gx·y), and the final Bitcoin private key is the scalar product x·

properties.value: Same logical asset as ALG-136e45af: one Aes.Create() per site immediately configured KeySize=256 and Mode=ECB for BIP38 key encryption. The generic rule recorded it with unstated size/mode; the specific rules (ALG-12f61078, ALG-136e45af) resolved both attributes.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BIP38 password KDF. Two parameter sets, both exactly as BIP38 requires: N=16384, r=8, p=8 for directly-encrypted keys (Bip38KeyPair.cs:92,272; Bip38Intermediate.cs:212) and the 1024,1,1,1 multiplier form for lot/sequence confirmation codes. scrypt is memory-hard and quantum-resistant in practice; the parameters are fixed by the BIP38 wire format, so not tunable without breaking interop.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Key-size attribute of the same AES-256-ECB BIP38 cipher object: the 256-bit key is the scrypt-derived second half (derivedhalf2), giving a 128-bit Grover margin. Mode is ECB per BIP38 — see ALG-136e45af for the mode posture.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The keygen randomness for this wallet generator: private keys, BIP38 owner entropy/salts, mini-keys, M-of-N splits and paper-wallet entropy all come from these CSPRNGs. Cryptographically secure — a posture strength, not a weakness; the '?' rating is 'practice', not risk. No weak System.Random found at these sites.
